section: Family - types, functions and changing structure in India
subsections: High-risk families and family problems - single-parent, dual-career, elderly care, family courts
Data on household size and family types (Census 2011, NFHS)

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT identified as a factor contributing to the rise of single-parent and female-headed households?
accepted.x: Widowhood, marital instability and male migration are identified as causes of rising single-parent and female-headed households. Expansion of joint-family residence is not listed as a cause.
accepted.tq: Find the option that reverses the stated causes rather than merely naming a related family feature.
accepted.sec: High-risk families and family problems - single-parent, dual-career, elderly care, family courts

accepted.s: In the context of dual-career urban households, which area is particularly subjected to pressure?
accepted.x: Dual-income urban households place pressure on child care and caregiving arrangements.
accepted.tq: Identify the direct functional consequence associated with the given household type.
accepted.sec: High-risk families and family problems - single-parent, dual-career, elderly care, family courts

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding elderly care in India:
1. It depends partly on filial piety.
2. Nuclearisation and migration can strain traditional family support.
3. Alternative care arrangements may therefore be needed.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Elderly care is linked to filial piety, while nuclearisation and migration weaken traditional support systems and create a need for alternative care.
accepted.tq: Accept the connected cause-effect chain when all three statements describe the same social process.
accepted.sec: High-risk families and family problems - single-parent, dual-career, elderly care, family courts

accepted.s: The Family Courts Act, 1984, followed the recommendations of which report?
accepted.x: The Family Courts Act, 1984 followed the 59th Law Commission Report of 1974.
accepted.tq: Link the statute to its specific recommending report and year.
accepted.sec: High-risk families and family problems - single-parent, dual-career, elderly care, family courts

accepted.s: As of 31 July 2025, how many family courts were functioning in how many States and Union Territories?
accepted.x: As of 31 July 2025, 953 family courts were running in 29 States and Union Territories.
accepted.tq: Match both numerical components; do not accept an option with only one correct figure.
accepted.sec: High-risk families and family problems - single-parent, dual-career, elderly care, family courts

accepted.s:
Under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, maintenance provisions cover which of the following?
1. Wives
2. Children
3. Indigent parents
4. Divorced wives
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The maintenance provisions under the BNSS, 2023 cover wives, children, indigent parents and divorced wives.
accepted.tq: Check the completeness of the statutory beneficiary list before choosing a partial combination.
accepted.sec: High-risk families and family problems - single-parent, dual-career, elderly care, family courts

accepted.s: According to Census data, the proportion of nuclear households in rural India changed from 2001 to 2011 as follows:
accepted.x: Rural nuclear households increased from 50.7% in 2001 to 52.1% in 2011.
accepted.tq: Separate the rural nuclear row from the urban and joint-household rows in the comparison table.
accepted.sec: Data on household size and family types (Census 2011, NFHS)

accepted.s: The proportion of joint households in rural India declined from 2001 to 2011 from:
accepted.x: Rural joint households declined from 20.1% in 2001 to 16.8% in 2011.
accepted.tq: Use the household-type and rural/urban labels together to avoid a row-column swap.
accepted.sec: Data on household size and family types (Census 2011, NFHS)

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the change in the proportion of nuclear households in urban India between 2001 and 2011?
accepted.x: Urban nuclear households declined from 54.3% in 2001 to 52.3% in 2011.
accepted.tq: Compare the correct geographic row before comparing the household category and direction of change.
accepted.sec: Data on household size and family types (Census 2011, NFHS)

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the change in urban joint households between 2001 and 2011?
accepted.x: The proportion of urban joint households declined from 16.5% in 2001 to 14.6% in 2011.
accepted.tq: Track both the direction and the exact endpoints instead of relying on the familiar percentage pair.
accepted.sec: Data on household size and family types (Census 2011, NFHS)

accepted.s: Which of the following statements is correct regarding household composition in India in 2011?
o: Less than one-fourth of all households were nuclear.
Urban nuclear households were absent from the Census classification.
Over half of all households were nuclear.
Joint households formed over half of all households.
accepted.x: More than half of all households were nuclear in 2011.
accepted.tq: Use the broad national conclusion rather than confusing it with a rural or urban percentage.
accepted.sec: Data on household size and family types (Census 2011, NFHS)

accepted.s: NFHS-6 (2023–24) was released by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare with which institution as the nodal agency?
o: International Institute for Population Sciences, Mumbai
accepted.x: NFHS-6 was released by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, with the International Institute for Population Sciences, Mumbai, as the nodal agency.
accepted.tq: Apply the institutional-role trap by distinguishing the releasing ministry from the nodal agency.
accepted.sec: Data on household size and family types (Census 2011, NFHS)

accepted.s: NFHS-6 (2023–24) covered approximately how many households and how many districts?
accepted.x: NFHS-6 covered 6.79 lakh households across 715 districts.
accepted.tq: Keep the sample-size figure and geographic-coverage figure distinct; the distractors reverse or alter them.
accepted.sec: Data on household size and family types (Census 2011, NFHS)

accepted.s: What was the total fertility rate reported by NFHS-6 for 2023–24?
accepted.x: NFHS-6 reported a total fertility rate of 2.0.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the overall NFHS-6 figure from the urban and rural NFHS-5 figures.
accepted.sec: Data on household size and family types (Census 2011, NFHS)

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding fertility rates reported in the National Family Health Surveys:
1. The urban total fertility rate in NFHS-5 was 1.6.
2. The rural total fertility rate in NFHS-5 was 2.1.
3. The total fertility rate in NFHS-6 was 2.0.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: NFHS-5 reported urban and rural fertility rates of 1.6 and 2.1 respectively, while NFHS-6 reported an overall rate of 2.0.
accepted.tq: Separate survey rounds and geographic categories before evaluating the numerical statements.
accepted.sec: Data on household size and family types (Census 2011, NFHS)

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
accepted.x: NFHS-6 relates to 2023–24 and reported a total fertility rate of 2.0. The other options incorrectly combine survey years and fertility figures.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure survey-year and figure pair, then eliminate cross-matched values.
accepted.sec: Data on household size and family types (Census 2011, NFHS)

accepted.s: Which of the following statements correctly reflects the recent position advocated by Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu?
o: Replacement of all joint families by nuclear households
A return to the joint family and incentives for families with two or more children
Complete abolition of family-based welfare measures
A compulsory one-child policy for every household
accepted.x: N. Chandrababu Naidu urged a return to the joint family and incentives for having two or more children in the context of declining fertility.
accepted.tq: Identify the policy position without extending it into an unsupported compulsory measure.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s:
With reference to the debate on the changing joint family, consider the following statements:
1. M.N. Srinivas, A.M. Shah and I.P. Desai are associated with discussions of the changing family structure.
2. Srinivas and Shah viewed the joint family mainly through the idea of continuity.
3. I.P. Desai linked the rise of nuclear households to capitalism.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Srinivas, Shah and Desai are associated with the debate; Srinivas and Shah emphasised continuity, while Marxist sociologist I.P. Desai linked nuclear households to capitalism.
accepted.tq: Check whether the scholars are correctly assigned to the continuity and capitalism arguments.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Who among the following is associated with the Marxist interpretation that nuclear households are linked to capitalism?
accepted.x: Marxist sociologist I.P. Desai linked the emergence of nuclear households to capitalism.
accepted.tq: Use the thinker-argument association rather than the broader topic association.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which statement regarding Andhra Pradesh and succession law is correct?
o: Andhra Pradesh enacted its succession amendment in 1985, before the central amendment of 2005.
Andhra Pradesh enacted its succession amendment in 2005, before the central amendment of 1985.
The central amendment preceded the Andhra Pradesh amendment by 20 years.
Both amendments were enacted in the same year.
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh made its succession amendment in 1985, which was 20 years before the central amendment of 2005.
accepted.tq: Arrange the two amendment years first, then verify the stated twenty-year difference.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s:
Arrange the following in chronological order from earliest to latest:
A. Andhra Pradesh succession amendment
B. Family Courts Act
C. Central succession amendment
D. NFHS-6
accepted.x: The Andhra Pradesh succession amendment was in 1985, followed by the Family Courts Act in 1984?
accepted.tq: Use the earliest and latest anchors first, then place the intermediate legal developments carefully.
accepted.sec: Universal angles
